clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau met a man in Beverly Hills worth a couple hundred million dollars and asked how he started.

A 650-square-foot studio apartment. A job earning $3,000 a month, plus nights and weekends on a side business.

The real secret wasn't the income - it was what he refused to do. He never raised his overhead as the money grew. He invested the difference and stayed near people already living where he wanted to go.

Hundreds of thousands became millions, then tens of millions. Most people never get there, because they raise their spending the moment they raise their income.

clips.end_words: mental training that you need to have
clips.send: A trader sends this to a friend who panics after selling too early - the exact mental fix, real relief from anxiety.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau once bought a stock at $2.50 a share. It shot up to $12 - six times his money - and he sold, thrilled with the win.

Then it kept climbing. $13, $14, $18, $19. He called a billionaire friend to vent about selling too soon.

His friend's answer: "Shut up. You made six times your money. Someone else bought your shares at $12 and now has a stock worth $19 - aren't you happy for him too?" The lesson: once you sell, stop watching the price.

Where in your life are you still watching a price you already cashed out of?

#kevintrudeau #investing #stockmarket #mindset #wealthmindset #money

Kevin Trudeau spent nearly a decade in prison with a man named Donnie French, who came out flat broke and owing a huge restitution.

A few years later, Donnie was worth hundreds of millions of dollars.

At a conference, someone who'd studied the law of attraction for twenty years asked how a guy starting from zero got there so fast while they had nothing to show for two decades of trying.

Kevin Trudeau says the answer is simple: Donnie was mad as hell about where he was, and he refused to stay there.

Kevin Trudeau interviewed manifestation expert Peter Sage, who said the first step to getting what you want is knowing exactly what you want.

Kevin disagreed on camera: "No, that's not the first step."

He says the real first step is getting disgusted with where you are - building what he calls contracted energy - before you can clearly define what you actually want. Most people skip that step and wonder why nothing moves.

Have you skipped straight to wishing without ever getting mad enough to change anything?
